candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is angioleiomyoma, a benign vascular smooth muscle neoplasm. Synovial chondromatosis is a completely different entity characterized by cartilaginous nodules arising from synovial metaplasia. The MRI features described (isointense to muscle on T1, heterogeneous on T2, peripheral rim enhancement, no fat signal) are more consistent with a soft tissue vascular/smooth muscle tumor than with synovial chondromatosis, which typically shows calcified loose bodies and chondroid signal characteristics. These two diagnoses share no diagnostic overlap.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Synovial chondromatosis is a distinct cartilaginous metaplastic condition of the synovium, not a vascular smooth muscle tumor (angioleiomyoma)

case_quality_flags: Angioleiomyoma is an uncommon intra-articular diagnosis; MRI features described (T1 isointense to muscle, T2 heterogeneous with internal specks, unremarkable on fat-sat T2, peripheral rim enhancement) are atypical for classic angioleiomyoma but are cited in rare case reports of intra-articular angioleiomyoma
No histopathological confirmation mentioned in the clinical record; diagnosis rests on imaging characteristics alone
